title: Notes on Facing Page

illustrates.quote: Notes on Facing Pages. Use combined print page numbers when transcribing text and notes printed on facing pages. Lettered continuation pages require the combined print page numbers. (See Sample 16-8: Notes on Facing Page on page 16-26.)

blocks.text:
143 resolv'd: convinced.
148 thorough: through. untrod state: new government.
155 presently: immediately.
158 still: always.
159 falls shrewdly: happens to an extreme degree. “My suspicions unfortunately are always accurate.”
blocks.features: A facing glossary page (left, unnumbered as running text) keyed entirely by print line numbers rather than symbols, facing the play-script text itself on the right-hand page.

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 16.7.7, illustrating notes and text printed on facing pages, requiring combined print page numbers in braille. This is a genuine excerpt: its braille line numbering begins at 20, not 1, matching the source page image.
print.printFeatures: Two facing print pages reproduced side by side: a plain glossary page on the left (line-number-keyed entries, no running prose) and the numbered play-script page (101) on the right.

pageBreaks.note: Explicit —New Braille Page— marker in the source, after the 6th line of this excerpt (source braille line 25); the line-number field restarts at 1 on the new page.

braille.notes: Genuine excerpt starting at braille line 20 (not 1), verified on the page image -- no earlier lines invented. Line-number field width 5 (max line number 25, two digits, +3). Each glossary entry begins with its print line number (e.g. #adc = 143, #aei = 159) rather than a symbol, per the facing-page glossary format; a combined page reference (b#ajj-#aja, i.e. 100-101 combined) appears right-flush at the end.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.7 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: Run A asserted 40; direct verification (lines 13117/13119, field width 5, digits(25)+3) finds 58-character lines -- the same tabbed-reference anomaly as example-16-10, explicitly named in the task brief for this file -- with no line reaching 40. Left null (overturning Run A, matching Run B). braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
